r0.why: White from loss of symbiotic algae and pigments [1]; temperature, light, salinity, nutrient stressors [2]; stressed, starvation/disease, risk of death [3].

r1.why: Zooxanthellae single-celled, in tissue, give colour [13]; photosynthetic nutrients crucial in clear nutrient-poor water [14]; CO2 and ammonium in return [15]; up to 90% of energy [23].

r2.why: Warm/cool water, high light, microbial disease break symbiosis [16]; polyp consumes or expels, pale or white [20,21]; colourful bleaching from intrinsic pigments [22]; starvation [23]; persisting conditions lower survival [24].

r3.why: Zooxanthellae must re-enter and restart photosynthesis [25]; starved polyps decay [26]; skeletons taken over by algae blocking regrowth [27]; erosion collapses reef [28].

r4.why: Leading cause rising temperature from climate change [4]; local vs global-warming triggered events [30]; ENSO heatwaves main cause [33]; IPCC 2022 sharp increase since early 1980s [36].

r5.why: GBR first major bleaching 1998, three events 2016-2020 [40,41]; 2016 killed 29-50% [8]; April 2024 NOAA fourth and largest [11]; Jan 2023-Sep 2025 ~84.4%, at least 83 countries [12].
